subject: Copywriting
title: Edward Bernays: The Father of PR
description: A fast breakdown of Edward Bernays: The Father of PR for builders.

hook.text: Edward Bernays, Freud's nephew, called propaganda 'the engineering of consent.' He made it respectable—and renamed it.

buildup.text: In 1929, Bernays staged 'Torches of Freedom'—women smoking in an Easter parade—to sell cigarettes as liberation.

discovery.text: He didn't advertise cigarettes. He advertised freedom. The product was irrelevant; the symbol was irresistible.

twist.text: Bernays proved that selling ideas is more powerful than selling products.

climax.text: His 1928 book 'Propaganda' argued that invisible rulers shape public opinion. He was both warning and teaching.

punchline.text: Freud's nephew sold cigarettes as freedom. He called it public relations.

quiz.question: What did Bernays call his 1929 campaign for women smoking?
